subject: different result between scanone and stepwiseqtl

messages.subject: different result between scanone and stepwiseqtl
parts:
Dear Dr Broman and list members,

Apologies in advance if you might consider my question as too simple to be asking... and I will be very gratful if someone could help me to understand my QTL results.

I have two major questions.

I work on a  4-way cross without X chromosome. I used scanone (method=c("mr", "hk")) to first survey major genomic regions associated to my traits.
After that, I used stepwiseqtl( method= "hk") with trait-specific penalties calculated based on 1000 permutations.

Serie 1.
For almost all my traits, the significant results of marker regression and interval mapping are consistent with results of multiple QTL model.
However, I observed that for some traits, the result was different between scanone and stepwiseqtl.
For example, for one phenotype, the scanone result showed two significant QTL in chromosomes 8 and 17 at alpha=0.05 level.
Stepwiseqtl fit a best model of 2 QTL located on chromosomes 5 and 17.
As it seems the 2-QTL model is the best for the phenotype, I used scantwo to investigate possible two-QTL model. The summary is as followed:

       pos1f pos2f lod.full lod.fv1 lod.int     pos1a pos2a lod.add lod.av1
c5:c17     1     7     11.4    5.55    1.36         7     6    10.1    4.19
c8:c17    36    38     12.6    6.68    2.88        39     6     9.7    3.80

with 5% threshold as c(12.0,9.82,8.85,6.99,3.78,3.99)

I conclued that the model with interaction is little probable with the small lod.int while 2 additive QTL model is more probable (lod.add > Tadd  & lod.av1>Tav1 for both of them).

It's true that the model including chromosomes 5 and 17 is faintly significant. As the question asked by scanone and multiple QTL model is not the same ( "Is there a QTL here?" v.s. " Are there QTL here, here ...and here?" ), could  I interpret the result as: "when considering the presence of major QTL in ch17, it's more probable to have an other QTL in ch5". But how abour the one in chromosome 8 identified via scanone?

 I also used fitqtl to access the model LOD score and %var of multiple QTL model, they are quite the same as you can see below:

###chr5 and 17
Full model result
---------------------------------- 
Model formula: y ~ Q1 + Q2

       df       SS        MS      LOD     %var
Model   6 166.5700 27.761672 10.09168 21.90167
Error 181 593.9658  3.281579                 
Total 187 760.5358                           


Drop one QTL at a time ANOVA table:
---------------------------------- 
       df Type III SS   LOD   %var F value
5...@7.0   3       64.39 4.201  8.466    6.54
1...@6.0  3      113.78 7.155 14.960   11.56


###chr8 and 17
Method: Haley-Knott regression
Model:  normal phenotype
Number of observations : 188

Full model result
---------------------------------- 
Model formula: y ~ Q1 + Q2

       df       SS        MS      LOD    %var
Model   6 160.6586 26.776437 9.687388 21.1244
Error 181 599.8772  3.314239                
Total 187 760.5358                          


Drop one QTL at a time ANOVA table:
---------------------------------- 
       df Type III SS   LOD   %var F value
8...@40.0  3       58.47 3.797  7.689    5.88
1...@6.0  3       76.72 4.913 10.088    7.72

Why the type III SS/LOD/%var for the QTL at chromosome 17 changed in these two models while it's the major locus?


Serie 2.
For several traits, I saturated the max.qtl =10 option and identified digenic epistasis each time when the max number of QTL is atteinded.
When I change the max.qtl option to 15, the model is always saturated. But when I made max.qtl=8, only 4 of 11 traits saturated the max.qtl criteria.
It seems to me that the way to figure out the most probable multiple QTL model in this case is to use my data and do a simulation to access the positions and interaction. But as I have 11 traits exhibit this profile, do you have a simpler idea for check or I can interpret as " a multigenic control" for these traits?


In advance, I would like to thank you for your patience and your advice.

Sincerley
Yung-Fen HUANG

> Why the type III SS/LOD/%var for the QTL at chromosome 17 changed in these two models while it's the major locus?

The percent variances explained by the QTL in these tables are calculated as a transformation of the LOD scores. As the LOD score for chr 17 when conditioned on chr 5 is higher than when conditioned on chr 8, the estimated percent variance explained is higher.

> Serie 2.
> For several traits, I saturated the max.qtl =10 option and identified digenic epistasis each time when the max number of QTL is atteinded.
> When I change the max.qtl option to 15, the model is always saturated. But when I made max.qtl=8, only 4 of 11 traits saturated the max.qtl criteria.

But as I have 11 traits exhibit this profile, do you have a simpler idea for check or I can interpret as " a multigenic control" for these traits?

I'm not sure what you mean by "saturated", but I would be cautious about models with very many QTL, particularly if some are tightly linked to each other. Also, I would study the stepwiseqtl results with different values of max.qtl.

karl
